title: Winganhauppauge
summary: An Islip brook-and-neck placename sometimes associated with Champlain's Creek, preserving a waterway name before later English naming.
ancestral_territory_note: Shown in relation to Secatogue Ancestral Land on the current ancestral territory map.
why_this_matters: The original Algonquian name Winganhauppauge, now commonly known as Champlain's Creek, specifically identified this productive brook and its headwaters in the town of Islip. Restoring the authentic Native vocabulary for Long Island's freshwater systems honors the deep ecological awareness of Indigenous communities who relied on these vital inland resources for their daily survival.
introduction_content: Winganhauppauge names an Islip brook and neck landscape. The older name appears to have belonged first to the brook or its headwaters, showing how water features often carried the place name before English records applied it more broadly to surrounding land.
